articles.title: Investigadores do voo da FlyDubai revelam que copiloto usou machado de emergência para atacar comandante | G1
articles.standfirst: Item obrigatório de segurança é mantido na cabine de comando de aeronaves comerciais para uso em situações de emergência, como acidentes ou incêndios.
articles.summary: Item obrigatório de segurança é mantido na cabine de comando de aeronaves comerciais para uso em situações de emergência, como acidentes ou incêndios.
articles.body:
Investigadores do voo da FlyDubai revelaram neste sábado (3) que o copiloto usou um machado que fazia parte do equipamento de segurança para atacar o comandante.

Investigadores tentavam determinar como o agressor conseguiu levar uma arma a bordo sem ser detectado. Agora, sabemos. Segundo o procurador-geral dos Emirados Árabes Unidos, o ataque foi com um machado de emergência - item obrigatório de segurança que é mantido na cabine de comando de aeronaves comerciais para uso em situações de emergência, como acidentes ou incêndios.

Investigadores do voo da FlyDubai revelam que copiloto usou machado de emergência para atacar — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

No voo FZ1073, da empresa FlyDubai, que tinha como destino Israel , o machado virou arma nas mãos do copiloto que tentou assumir o controle do avião. Mesmo ferido, o piloto Smit Machchhar, da Índia, conseguiu destrancar a porta da cabine, permitindo que tripulantes e passageiros entrassem para conter o agressor e estabilizar a aeronave, que tinha despencado 5 mil metros em 30 segundos.

Pela primeira vez, autoridades dos Emirados Árabes classificaram o incidente como uma tentativa de ato terrorista. As investigações em curso precisam esclarecer, agora, se o copiloto, um cidadão de Omã, agiu como um lobo solitário ou se tem alguma ligação com grupos extremistas. A imprensa internacional, citando fontes, noticiou que, antes de ser contratado pela FlyDubai, o copiloto, de 29 anos, havia sido impedido de voar no seu país de origem devido a preocupações de que tivesse se radicalizado.

Na sexta-feira (2), visivelmente emocionado em uma videochamada com o primeiro-ministro da Índia, o piloto-herói disse que fez um último esforço, enquanto era atacado, porque não poderia permitir que todos a bordo morressem.

articles.title: Guarda Costeira encontra destroços de avião médico desaparecido nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Aeronave havia saído das Bermudas e tinha Boston como destino, segundo autoridades. De acordo com a Guarda Costeira, o avião modelo Gulfstream G100 transportava dois membros de uma equipe médica, um paciente e um parente dele.
articles.summary: Aeronave havia saído das Bermudas e tinha Boston como destino, segundo autoridades. De acordo com a Guarda Costeira, o avião modelo Gulfstream G100 transportava dois membros de uma equipe médica, um paciente e um parente dele.
articles.body:
Membros da Guarda Costeira Americana realizam buscas na costa de Nantucket, em Massachusetts. — Foto: Guarda Costeira dos EUA via AFP

As equipes de busca encontraram um "campo de destroços" na costa de Nantucket, em Massachusetts, de uma ambulância aérea que transportava seis pessoas quando desapareceu sobre o Oceano Atlântico neste sábado (3), durante um voo das Bermudas para Boston, informou a Guarda Costeira dos Estados Unidos.

Quatro canadenses e dois cidadãos das Bermudas estavam a bordo, e seus familiares foram notificados enquanto as buscas continuavam, informou a Guarda Costeira em comunicado. A corporação acrescentou que uma de suas embarcações permaneceria nas buscas durante a noite e ao longo do domingo.

Segundo a Guarda Costeira, a Administração Federal de Aviação (FAA) informou que o Gulfstream G100 perdeu contato nas primeiras horas da manhã de sábado. Áudios do controle de tráfego aéreo indicam que a aeronave pode ter ficado "voando às cegas" quando uma tempestade surgiu à frente, pouco antes de desaparecer.

O piloto relatou problemas elétricos e declarou emergência enquanto o jato se aproximava da costa, de acordo com gravações do controle de tráfego aéreo publicadas pelo site LiveATC.net. Em um dos trechos, é possível ouvir um controlador perguntando: "Entendido, você disse que está voando às cegas. Foi isso que você disse?"

Isso leva Mary Schiavo, ex-inspetora-geral do Departamento de Transportes dos Estados Unidos, a acreditar que o avião pode ter perdido seus instrumentos de navegação justamente quando uma tempestade cruzava sua rota, conforme mostravam os radares. Dados preliminares do site de rastreamento FlightRadar24 indicam ainda que a aeronave desceu rapidamente de sua altitude de cruzeiro, de cerca de 24 mil pés, para aproximadamente 10 mil pés.

"Algo grave aconteceu com essa queda brusca, e eles entraram nessa grande tempestade. É um lugar terrível para perder os instrumentos e estar voando às cegas", afirmou Schiavo, que atua como advogada especializada em aviação. "É muito fácil ficar desorientado e não saber se está virando, subindo, descendo, etc."

O jato ambulância aérea registrado no Canadá transportava quatro tripulantes e dois passageiros quando decolou do Aeroporto Internacional L.F. Wade, nas Bermudas, para o voo noturno rumo a Massachusetts, segundo comunicado da Skyport, operadora do aeroporto.

O ministro dos Transportes do Canadá, Steven MacKinnon, afirmou na rede social X que o governo canadense estava acompanhando de perto o caso e trabalhando com as autoridades nas operações de busca e resgate.

O Conselho Nacional de Segurança nos Transportes dos Estados Unidos (NTSB) informou que estava reunindo informações sobre a ocorrência, mas não disse imediatamente se abriria uma investigação.

articles.title: Eleitores do DF têm se interessado menos por política, aponta pesquisa da UnB; veja dados | G1
articles.standfirst: Cerca de 44% dos entrevistados definem conversas sobre a campanha como 'estressantes' e 'frustrantes'.
articles.summary: Cerca de 44% dos entrevistados definem conversas sobre a campanha como 'estressantes' e 'frustrantes'.
articles.body:
Um levantamento feito pelo grupo de pesquisa Observa DF, vinculado à Universidade de Brasília, mostra que os moradores do Distrito Federal se dizem "decepcionados" e pessimistas com relação à política.

Segundo o relatório divulgado nesta semana:

36% dos eleitores da capital se dizem muito interessados ou interessados em política;

Dados do Latin American Public Opinion Project (Lapop) indicam que, no Brasil, a média de eleitores com "muito ou algum" interesse em política é de 53%. Ou seja: a média do interesse nacional por política é 17 pontos percentuais superior aos resultados do DF .

Apesar do cenário pessimista em relação à política, o Distrito Federal, sede dos poderes da República, demonstra interesse maior pelo período eleitoral .

Segundo a pesquisa, 41% dos entrevistados afirmam ter muito ou algum interesse nas campanhas .

Ao g1 , um dos coordenadores do levantamento, o cientista político e professor da Universidade de Brasília (UnB) Lucio Rennó, explica o contraste entre o interesse pelas eleições e o desalento com a política em geral .

"Isso tem a ver com um certo desânimo que vem do acirramento dos conflitos causados por uma polarização acentuada. A discussão política ficou muito conflituosa, dividida em dois grupos muito claros, e isso de certa maneira afasta as pessoas do debate, porque esse debate fica muito baseado no desentendimento e na agressão. Então afasta as pessoas de se envolverem e se engajarem", observa Rennó.

Lucas Faria, 22 anos, diz que seu desinteresse por política começou ao perceber que não encontrava candidatos que representassem seus valores.

Segundo ele, as propostas costumam se repetir e a polarização agravou esse cenário.

"Eu sinto que o cenário está muito dividido, sabe? É muito polarizado, então a maioria só enxerga dois lados e acaba que a gente continua na mesma espiral. A gente poderia procurar algo novo, mas costuma ser esse argumento, né? De que só dois lados podem vencer, então você tem que usar o voto útil", afirma o estudante de educação física.

Menos eleitores nas campanhas presenciais

Apesar da polarização e do desencanto com a política, o consumo de notícias sobre o tema permanece elevado.

A pesquisa mostra que 41% dos entrevistados acompanham diariamente informações políticas , o mesmo percentual registrado para o interesse nas campanhas eleitorais.

Já a participação direta nas atividades de campanha é menor. O levantamento aponta que 33% dos eleitores acompanharam pouco de perto os pleitos .

"O processo de campanha eleitoral vem mudando. As pessoas hoje não se engajam mais tanto em atividades presenciais. Então, ir a um comício, usar material de campanha, participar de reunião, todas essas atividades são menos frequentes do que você isoladamente buscar informações na televisão, nos meios de comunicação tradicionais, na internet", explica Rennó.

Segundo o pesquisador, o levantamento mostra uma mudança na forma como os eleitores se relacionam com as campanhas.

"A campanha [eleitoral] está mudando, e eu acho que a nossa pesquisa capta essa mudança também", completa.

De acordo com o relatório, os meios mais utilizados pelos brasilienses para se informar sobre política são:

os noticiários, citados por 36% dos entrevistados;

as redes sociais, mencionadas por 28% – nesse grupo, 40% citou o Instagram

A estudante de direito Sofia Melo, de 22 anos, também relata frustração com a campanha eleitoral. Assim como Lucas, ela percebe um crescente desinteresse dos eleitores pelo processo político.

"Olhando as campanhas eleitorais, os materiais de campanha, os debates, que, honestamente, eu parei já de acompanhar de um mês para cá. Eu sinto que os candidatos não estão interessados em debater políticas públicas."

Para Sofia, a polarização prejudica a troca de ideias e dificulta a formação de consciência política entre os eleitores. "O debate [polarizado] é muito prejudicial para a formação de consciência política dentro da população."

O relatório também aponta que os jovens estão entre os grupos mais suscetíveis às chamadas bolhas informacionais, em razão do maior grau de conexão com as redes sociais.

🔎 Bolhas informacionais são um fenômeno associado ao funcionamento das plataformas digitais. Os algoritmos tendem a priorizar conteúdos alinhados aos interesses e preferências dos usuários, o que reduz o contato com opiniões divergentes e reforça percepções já existentes.

Apesar desse cenário, Sofia afirma que busca informações principalmente na imprensa profissional .

"Porque não dá para confiar no que você recebe de amigos, de conhecidos, porque a gente já sabe, né? Reiteradamente, que existe uma indústria de notícias falsas, de notícias tendenciosas."

A pesquisa indica que a desconfiança também se reflete nas conversas sobre política.

Quando perguntados sobre como têm sido os diálogos a respeito da campanha eleitoral:

44% dos entrevistados classificaram essas conversas como estressantes ou frustrantes ;

28% disseram que elas são interessantes e informativas;

28% afirmaram não conversar sobre política.

Os sentimentos positivos em relação ao cenário político também aparecem, mas em menor proporção. Apenas 36% dos entrevistados disseram se sentir esperançosos e 29%, entusiasmados com a política brasileira.

A pesquisa ouviu mil eleitores residentes no Distrito Federal entre os dias 7 e 15 de setembro de 2026. A amostra foi distribuída por 29 pontos de coleta, agrupados em cinco faixas de renda das regiões administrativas do DF, da renda mais alta à mais baixa.

O levantamento tem nível de confiança de 95% e margem de erro de aproximadamente 3,1 pontos percentuais.

articles.summary: NOIDA: A 28-year-old software engineer died by suicide after jumping from the balcony of a 41st-floor Airbnb in Supernova in Sector 94 on Saturday morning.
articles.body: NOIDA: A 28-year-old software engineer died by suicide after jumping from the balcony of a 41st-floor Airbnb in Supernova in Sector 94 on Saturday morning.A team of AC mechanics working at a nearby flat spotted him hanging from the balcony railing and tried to persuade him to step back. He allegedly told them he was "depressed", before jumping off the edge.Police identified the man as Sambhav Jain, a resident of IMT Manesar who worked for a private company in Gurgaon. He had checked into the Airbnb in Spira tower alone around 3pm on Friday and ordered food online that evening.Two videos of the incident have emerged. One, recorded by a resident of the 17th floor of another tower, shows Jain falling off the balcony. The other, filmed by a member of the AC repair team from a nearby balcony, captures the technicians trying to communicate with him before he jumps."No sooner did we receive information, a team from Sector 126 police station reached the spot and identified the man with the help of ID cards found in his room," said Sumnesh Kumar, SHO of Sector 126.Kumar said Jain had left home around three days ago and stayed at hotels in different places before arriving in Noida. Police are examining WhatsApp conversations between Jain and his father over a monetary dispute"According to the chats, it appeared that his father insisted he return home, but he refused. He said he would repay all the debts first," Kumar said.Police are also examining if personal difficulties, too, may have contributed to his death. The SHO said Jain had married about two years ago, but the relationship ended in a divorce after a few months. Around that time, the couple's baby was born prematurely, and treatment costs reportedly exceeded Rs 30 lakh.Jain, police said, had borrowed money to meet the expenses. At Supernova, a team of police and officials from forensic science laboratory (FSL) inspected the scene and collected evidence. articles.body: Yemen's internationally recognised government has launched strikes against Iran-aligned Houthi targets in the capital Sanaa and the northern province of Saada, escalating military operations against the rebels amid growing tensions over control of the Red Sea.According to Reuters, Yemen's armed forces said they were conducting strikes against what they described as “vital targets” in Houthi-held areas. Houthi-run Al Masirah television, meanwhile, reported that Saudi Arabia had carried out an attack on Sanaa, although Riyadh had not immediately confirmed the claim.Yemen's armed forces said early on Sunday that they were conducting strikes against Iran-aligned Houthi forces in the capital Sanaa and the Houthi stronghold of Saada.The latest strikes mark a renewed escalation between the Saudi-backed Yemeni government and the Houthis. Fighting between the two sides had largely stopped after a 2022 truce, but hostilities resumed this year after the Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in July and began attacking Saudi territory and shipping.Saudi Arabia has responded with airstrikes in Yemen while backing government forces fighting to push back the Houthis, according to Reuters.Houthi-run Al Masirah TV reported that Saudi Arabia had carried out an attack on Sanaa. Reuters said there was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia of the reported attack.The Houthi claim came amid a wider escalation with Saudi Arabia. On October 3, the Houthis also claimed they had attacked an Aramco facility in Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, describing the strike as retaliation for Saudi-led attacks on Sanaa and other parts of Yemen.Saudi Arabia plans major offensiveThe latest strikes come as Saudi Arabia prepares for a potentially much larger military operation against the Houthis. Reuters reported that Riyadh is considering an offensive aimed at reversing recent Houthi gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast and regaining control of the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait.The planned operation would be led on the ground by Yemeni forces overseen by Saudi Arabia and supported by Saudi airstrikes. According to six regional and Western officials cited by Reuters, more than 100,000 Yemeni troops could be mobilised, depending on the scale of the offensive.Saudi officials are considering either a narrowly focused assault around Bab el-Mandeb or a broader, multi-front campaign involving coordinated attacks in Al-Bayda, Marib, Taiz and Al-Jawf. articles.summary: DEHRADUN: The 18km trek to Kedarnath, at 11,755 feet, from Gaurikund is for most pilgrims a journey of a lifetime in search of peace and tranquillity.
articles.body: DEHRADUN: The 18km trek to Kedarnath, at 11,755 feet, from Gaurikund is for most pilgrims a journey of a lifetime in search of peace and tranquillity.And now, in an unusual act of service, thousands, in perhaps a first, are returning with bags of plastic waste collected from the sacred site.Under the local administration's 'Carry Me Back' initiative, close to 5,000 pilgrims have so far voluntarily carried down more than 12 tonnes of compressed plastic waste, turning what began as a local effort to tackle the mounting garbage problem into a wider campaign.The move comes against the backdrop of a serious sanitation challenge at the shrine, where a huge visitor influx generates vast quantities of waste. Poor waste segregation, difficult weather and logistical limitations of working at such high altitudes compound everything.Social media has helped. Among the sights seen during the campaign have been pilgrims from Tamil Nadu, Odisha and other southern states carrying up to 10kg of trash on bicycles.Madan Lal, who had one arm amputated, carried a bag full of garbage with his healthy hand all the way to Gaurikund. Ankita Singh (28) who works in Gurgaon, brought back 8kg of waste along with two friends."When we set out from Gurgaon, our plans were different and did not include Kedarnath. However, we ended up coming here. articles.title: A radioactive material facility polluted an Illinois creek for decades; the 6.7-mile Superfund site has now been removed from the cleanup list
articles.summary: A 6.7-mile stretch of creek and river in DuPage County, Illinois, has reached a major milestone after decades of radioactive contamination linked to a
articles.body: A 6.7-mile stretch of creek and river in DuPage County, Illinois, has reached a major milestone after decades of radioactive contamination linked to a former industrial facility. The US Environmental Protection Agency deleted the Kerr-McGee Kress Creek/West Branch DuPage River Superfund site from the National Priorities List in August 2026, meaning the site no longer requires further Superfund response action to protect human health and the environment. The contamination was linked to the former Rare Earths Facility in West Chicago, which operated from 1932 to 1973 and processed rare earth elements and radioactive materials, as well as producing gas lantern mantles. Radioactive surface runoff from the facility entered Kress Creek, while thorium-containing material spread through the sediment and banks of the creek and the West Branch of the DuPage River, as well as some surrounding floodplain areas. This remarkable environmental recovery demonstrates how sustained, decades-long remediation efforts can successfully restore contaminated waterways, offering communities renewed confidence in their local ecosystems' long-term health and safety.How the Rare Earths Facility contaminated Kress CreekThe former facility was operated by Lindsay Light and Chemical Company and later by other companies, including Kerr-McGee. Its operations involved processing rare earth ores and radioactive materials, including thorium. Waste generated during those activities became part of a much larger environmental cleanup in the West Chicago area.The Kress Creek site was placed on the National Priorities List in 1991. EPA describes the Superfund site as covering approximately 6.7 miles, including Kress Creek and the West Branch of the DuPage River. Radioactively contaminated material was found in creek sediments, along streambanks and in portions of the floodplain. The contamination was part of a wider legacy from the former Rare Earths Facility. Four separate West Chicago-area sites associated with radioactive waste from the facility were ultimately placed on the National Priorities List.Crews removed contaminated soil and sedimentMajor cleanup work at Kress Creek began in 2005. EPA records describe the removal of contaminated soil and sediment from sections of Kress Creek and the West Branch of the DuPage River, followed by restoration of the affected areas. EPA's site profile says more than 129,000 cubic yards of contaminated material were removed during the cleanup. EPA's site profile dates the end of cleanup to October 2012, while the agency's September 3, 2026 release says cleanup was completed in 2014, with restoration continuing until 2025. An Illinois EPA page concerning the proposed deletion also gives October 2012 as the completion date.The cleanup was carried out section by section. Crews removed contaminated material from each area and then restored the affected sections with clean backfill and vegetation. Restoration work continued as the project progressed and remained underway after the cleanup phase, ultimately continuing through 2025. EPA and local officials marked the site's recent delisting at an event at McDowell Grove on September 3, 2026.Kress Creek was one of four Superfund sitesThe Kress Creek site was one of four National Priorities List sites created to address radioactive contamination associated with the former Rare Earths Facility. EPA says the Reed-Keppler Park site was deleted from the National Priorities List in 2010, followed by the Sewage Treatment Plant site in 2013. Kress Creek became the third of the four sites to be deleted.The Residential Areas site has also undergone cleanup but remains on the National Priorities List until the former Rare Earths Facility is addressed under the oversight of the Illinois Emergency Management Agency. The broader cleanup has therefore taken place in stages rather than as a single project. The Kress Creek delisting represents the completion of the Superfund process for that particular waterway and its associated contaminated areas.What National Priorities List deletion meansRemoval from the National Priorities List does not necessarily mean that every trace of historical contamination has disappeared from an area. Rather, deletion indicates that EPA has determined that the site no longer requires further Superfund response action based on the cleanup completed there. EPA proposed removing Kress Creek from the National Priorities List in March 2026 and formally deleted the site in August. EPA and local officials subsequently held the September 3 event in DuPage County to mark the recent delisting.The Illinois Department of Natural Resources, which discusses Kress Creek as part of the state's natural resource trustee work, says the original source of the radioactive contamination has been addressed so that additional thorium is no longer entering the environment from the former facility. For communities around West Chicago and DuPage County, the delisting represents the latest stage in a cleanup that has stretched across decades. Contaminated material was removed from the creek and river system, affected areas were restored, and the federal government has now formally taken Kress Creek off the National Priorities List. The history of the site nevertheless illustrates how contamination from an industrial operation can persist long after the facility itself has stopped operating. The former Rare Earths Facility closed decades ago, but its radioactive legacy required years of investigation, excavation, disposal and restoration before the Kress Creek Superfund site could reach its 2026 delisting.You use AI every day. What is so special about ACP Vivek Bhagat because of whom you are protecting him so much?" Das said.He alleged that police had been told that they could take time to examine video footage if required, but said the protesters expected an FIR to be registered by noon on October 4."We have told them that if you want time to watch the video then you can take time, but tomorrow (i.e. today, October 4) you will have time till 12. And after that the entire journalist community and the other protesters will come in the support of the police again outside the police station and will take a copy of the FIR," Das said.He added, "We will ensure that this ACP Vivek Bhagat, who is a monster in his uniform, gets a FIR against him."CJP protests against Gyanesh Kumar continueThe latest demand comes amid CJP-led protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Delhi Police on Saturday registered three FIRs in connection with the October 2 protests by student organisations, political parties and civil society activists who attempted to gather at Jantar Mantar.No individual or organisation was named as an accused in those FIRs, police said.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has since announced a fresh mobilisation in Delhi on October 10, saying the group would bring young Indians to the capital and march to Jantar Mantar.The CJP has also faced police action over its October 2 protest in Mumbai, with an FIR registered against organisers and 400-500 unidentified supporters over alleged unlawful assembly, traffic disruption and use of loudspeakers without permission.CJP has earlier raised police-action allegationsThe latest allegation follows other complaints by CJP supporters over police conduct during recent protests.The party had previously sought stricter charges in a case involving injuries allegedly sustained by a CJP supporter during a Jantar Mantar protest.Police have also faced allegations of excessive force during the recent protests, including an AAP-shared video that purportedly showed a Delhi Police officer punching a detained protester.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: ‘You’re coming in blind?’ Chilling audio before medical jet carrying 6 vanished over Atlantic
articles.summary: A medical evacuation jet disappeared over the Atlantic after reporting an emergency and electrical problems, losing radio and radar contact while
articles.body: A medical evacuation jet disappeared over the Atlantic after reporting an emergency and electrical problems, losing radio and radar contact while approaching Massachusetts. The US Coast Guard later found a debris field linked to the aircraft off Nantucket.According to Reuters, the Canadian registered Gulfstream G100 operated by Latitude Air Ambulance left Bermuda’s LF Wade International Airport at around 12.41am local time on Saturday. It was headed for Boston Logan International Airport with six people on board.A chilling audio clip captured the final moments before the jet disappeared over the Atlantic.Air traffic control recordings posted by LiveATC.net captured the final exchanges. The controller asked the pilot, “Roger, you said you’re coming in blind. Is that what you said?” The pilot’s response was not clearly audible. The controller then asked whether the crew was declaring an emergency.According to the Boston Globe, the aircraft was dealing with an electrical problem shortly before contact was lost. Emergency crews at Boston Logan were told the plane had lost radio and radar contact while approaching the area south of Nantucket.Reuters reported that the Gulfstream had been flying at around 24,000 feet before dropping about 13,000 feet in roughly two minutes. The Associated Press also reported that the aircraft descended to around 10,000 feet before contact was lost.The rapid descent came as the aircraft approached the Massachusetts coast. The Boston Globe reported that the plane was around 80 miles south of Nantucket when emergency crews at Logan were told to prepare for its arrival. It never reached Boston.The FAA issued a search and rescue alert at around 1.20am, according to the Boston Globe. The US Coast Guard then launched aircraft and vessels to search the waters south of Nantucket.The Coast Guard later confirmed that it had found a “debris field” from the missing medical flight. The debris was located south of Nantucket and was confirmed to be associated with the aircraft. Search operations for the six people on board continued.The Coast Guard said the search had covered about 1,644 square miles by the time the debris was located, according to the Nantucket Current. The discovery provided investigators with physical evidence of the aircraft’s final location.The six people on board included two pilots, two medical personnel, a patient and the patient’s relative. The four crew members were Canadian, while the two passengers were from Bermuda, according to the Canadian Press report carried by Stratford Today.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: China has accused a US congressional panel of spreading “blatant lies” after the committee criticised Starbucks for opening its first stores in Xinjiang,
articles.body: China has accused a US congressional panel of spreading “blatant lies” after the committee criticised Starbucks for opening its first stores in Xinjiang, where Washington has accused Beijing of genocide against the Uyghur minority.Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said the US House Select Committee on China was “fabricating claims out of thin air for political purposes” and had no credibility to comment on the situation in the region.“The so-called ‘genocide’ in Xinjiang is a blatant lie,” Guo said.His remarks came after committee chairman John Moolenaar called Starbucks’ decision to open two outlets in Urumqi, the capital of Xinjiang, “morally bankrupt” and urged the company to shut them.Starbucks opens first Xinjiang storesStarbucks opened two cafes in Urumqi this week, one at the city’s international airport and another at the Grand Bazaar, a popular tourist and shopping destination.Moolenaar said the move tied an American brand to what he described as the Chinese Communist Party’s “brutal campaign” against Uyghurs.“There is no justifiable reason for an American company to do business in a region where the CCP has detained more than a million Uyghurs and is stripping them of their faith, language, and culture,” he said in a statement.China rejects accusations of widespread abuses in Xinjiang, saying its policies in the region are aimed at combating terrorism, separatism and religious extremism.Guo said Xinjiang today enjoys “social stability, economic prosperity, ethnic unity and religious harmony”.He added that China would continue to expand high-standard opening-up and create more opportunities for foreign companies to invest and grow in the country.Xinjiang rights allegationsThe US and other governments have accused China of serious rights abuses against Uyghurs and other predominantly Muslim minorities in Xinjiang, while Beijing has repeatedly denied the allegations.A 2022 United Nations assessment said Chinese authorities may have committed crimes against humanity in the region and referred to the detention of more than a million Uyghurs and other Muslim minorities.Rights groups have also accused Chinese authorities of continuing to use forced labour in Xinjiang.The competing claims have become a major source of tension between Beijing and Washington, with the US formally describing China's treatment of Uyghurs as genocide.Starbucks has said it will continue investing in Xinjiang. articles.title: 'We don’t do background checks on foreign pilots': Israeli minister on flydubai incident
articles.summary: Israel’s transportation ministry said on Saturday that it does not conduct background checks on foreign pilots flying into the country and cannot
articles.body: Israel’s transportation ministry said on Saturday that it does not conduct background checks on foreign pilots flying into the country and cannot guarantee that flights operated by foreign airlines will be “100 percent” safe.The ministry’s security division said it does not receive the names of pilots and crew in advance and does not have the ability to conduct background checks on foreign pilots flying into Israel.“We are not an intelligence body that checks the intelligence background of foreigners,” a representative of the division said, according to Ynet. “We have no forces abroad. We have no staff that checks every person there.”The statements came after multiple reports that pilots from hostile states have repeatedly flown planes into Israel despite regulations intended to prevent them from doing so. The perpetrator of the terror attack on the flydubai flight, Hamam al-Hammami, was a citizen of Oman, which does not have relations with Israel.The security division said it could not specify how many pilots from hostile states had landed in Israel and that background checks were outsourced to the airlines themselves.“Nothing is 100% when it comes to security,” the division’s representative said, according to Ynet.This comes as questions mount over what could have been done to prevent the near-disaster involving flydubai Flight 1073.Channel 12 quoted the representative as saying the ministry could not guarantee “100% that this won’t happen again,” and that the only foolproof way to prevent such threats would be to prohibit foreign airlines from landing in Israel.Transportation Minister Miri Regev told the Kan public broadcaster that assessing the security of air travel falls under the responsibility of Israel’s security establishment.“Those who are supposed to say what the threat level is, and whether you can travel to a given destination, are security officials,” she said.Israel has said it has agreements with foreign airlines to prevent pilots from countries with which it has no diplomatic ties from flying into the country. Israel and Oman do not have formal diplomatic relations.Separately, a regional official and a person familiar with the matter said the co-pilot had been barred from flying by Oman over concerns that he had adopted extremist views. The official said he was subsequently moved to an administrative role at Oman Air, as cited by AP.The co-pilot was later hired by UAE-based Flydubai, the person familiar with the matter said. It was not immediately clear how extensively he was vetted before being hired.A Gulf diplomat said he underwent standard security checks, but these appeared to have focused on whether he had any criminal convictions rather than examining his background for possible signs of radicalisation.The regional official said security agencies from four countries in the region were working to determine the co-pilot’s motives, with assistance from the United States and other Western governments. The investigation has not concluded, but the Gulf diplomat said it had so far found no links to militant groups, suggesting the co-pilot may have acted alone.The regional official said the co-pilot was born in the UAE and that his mother is Syrian. He obtained Omani nationality through his father, who was also an Omani national. The official also said the co-pilot had travelled to Syria, without providing further details.Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday that the co-pilot had undergone “Islamist radicalization,” but provided no evidence.The flydubai flight made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after an extreme descent that tore away part of the aircraft’s rudder, prompting aviation experts to say it was fortunate not to crash. Flydubai said crew members travelling as passengers helped stabilise the aircraft and land safely.Captain Machcchar was seriously injured in the incident. The captain and co-pilot were later taken to the UAE, while the passengers, most of them Israeli, returned home on a separate flight later on Wednesday.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ‘He was so scared’: SP MP on ally Rahul Gandhi skipping Amethi in 2024 Lok Sabha polls
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Strain deepened within the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance ahead of Uttar Pradesh polls, with SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel in an off-the-cuff
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Strain deepened within the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance ahead of Uttar Pradesh polls, with SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel in an off-the-cuff remark claimed that Rahul Gandhi was "reluctant to contest the 2024 Lok Sabha election" from Amethi and chose Raebareli because he was "so scared".Patel, who represents Pratapgarh, also credited the SP-Congress alliance for the Congress's six Lok Sabha wins in Uttar Pradesh, arguing that the party would have drawn a blank in the state without SP's support.Speaking to news agency PTI, Patel said the SP leadership had to persuade Gandhi to contest from Raebareli after he appeared unwilling to fight from Amethi, the traditional Gandhi family constituency."Had there been no alliance (with the Samajwadi Party), they (Congress) wouldn't have won a single seat. It even reached a point where their top leader Rahul Gandhi was ready to give up his seat. He contested from elsewhere (Raebareli) instead of Amethi. He was so scared," he said.The leader futher added: "It was our national president who reassured and persuaded him, asking him to contest and warning that if he didn't, he (Akhilesh) would field his own candidate. Only then did Gandhi agree to contest. Otherwise, he was extremely reluctant to run for that traditional seat, the one said to belong to the Nehru family. Gandhi only managed to win it because of that persuasion," he said.Patel credits SP for Congress winsPatel said SP voters backed Congress candidates in constituencies allotted to the Congress under the alliance arrangement."Every single vote from the Samajwadi Party went to the Congress wherever they were allotted seats. That is precisely how they managed to win those six seats," he said.The SP won 37 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 elections, while Congress won six. The BJP won 33 seats, while the NDA's tally in the state stood at 36.Patel said the difference in the two parties' performances should be reflected in any future seat-sharing discussions."We secured 37 seats. We are far ahead of the Congress in every respect. They shouldn't ask for more than 50, and should feel happy. The Congress should cooperate, rather than making all sorts of absurd or negative remarks," Patel said.SP MP dismisses Congress's caste strategyPatel also criticised the Congress's reported caste strategy in Uttar Pradesh, including its appointment of a Brahmin as state Congress president and a Muslim as working president."This will not yield any benefit. Look, Dalits were with Mayawati, but they have now shifted to our side. They realised that there was no significant upliftment of Dalits during the Congress regime, and certainly none is happening under the BJP. Whereas, during the Samajwadi Party's tenure, everyone gets equal opportunities. Everyone gets an equal chance to progress; their children get a chance to receive an education."He added, "That is precisely why the party was named 'Samajwadi'. Our party operates based on the ideals of (Ram Manohar) Lohia-ji. Our party's objective is the welfare of all sections of society."The SP currently has 101 MLAs in the 403-member Uttar Pradesh Assembly, while Congress has two.Patel said the SP could benefit from continuing its alliance with Congress, but argued that the Congress would suffer more if it contested elections without its regional ally."If we proceed with an alliance, we will certainly benefit. Even if it doesn't happen, we won't have any significant loss. But for them, the tally will drop to zero. I can say this with confidence: if they don't contest as part of an alliance, they will end up with zero seats. The public will realise they are fielding candidates solely to split votes. If they act as vote-spoilers, they will be reduced to zero," Patel said.Congress hits backUttar Pradesh Congress spokesperson Anshu Awasthi pushed back against Patel's remarks and said the SP should rein in leaders making such statements."The Samajwadi Party must work to rein in leaders who make such statements. It is because of the INDIA bloc that he (Patel) has become an MP. He should know his limits and avoid making statements like these," Awasthi told PTI.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: PUNE: The plan to kill realtor Ketan Agarwal at Lohagad Fort in Pune district allegedly took shape after his fiancé Siya Goyal and her alleged lover
articles.body: PUNE: The plan to kill realtor Ketan Agarwal at Lohagad Fort in Pune district allegedly took shape after his fiancé Siya Goyal and her alleged lover Chetan Chaudhary studied online reports about the death of a young woman at the same location in 2025, according to the chargesheet filed by Pune Rural police before the Wadgaon Maval court.Agarwal, 26, died on June 18. The death was initially believed to be an accidental fall from Lohagad Fort, but the subsequent investigation found that he had allegedly been pushed.The 5,053-page chargesheet, filed on September 19, names Goyal, Chaudhary and Ritesh Hange as accused in the murder case. It cites mobile phone data, call detail records, social media material, messages, photographs, witness statements and technical analysis certificates as evidence.Fiancée allegedly did not want to marry AgarwalAccording to the chargesheet, Goyal did not want to marry Agarwal, with whom she got engaged on February 19 this year.Police allege that she subsequently conspired with Chaudhary and Hange to eliminate Agarwal and make his death appear to be an accident.The chargesheet says Goyal and Chaudhary searched Google, YouTube and social media platforms for information about deaths, trekking incidents and ways of concealing evidence.From 'Sonam Case' to deleting phone dataPolice have claimed that the accused also searched for information about the Meghalaya honeymoon murder of Raja Raghuvanshi, along with ways to delete phone and online data.Among the searches cited in the chargesheet were terms such as “Death Cap Mushroom India”, “Women Kills Family by Mushroom”, “Easy way to kill someone”, “Sonam Case”, “Lohagad Fort”, “How to format iPhone - No history on calls”, “How to Delete Google Account”, “Trekking Incident” and “How not to get manipulated”.The Mansi Govindpurkar caseA key part of the alleged planning involved the death of Mansi Govindpurkar, a 21-year-old woman from Sangvi who went missing on March 18, 2025 after leaving home saying she was going to college.Her last mobile location was traced to Lohagad. CCTV footage showed her arriving alone in a taxi and entering the fort. A search operation involving police and the Shivdurg rescue team found her body two days later in bushes near the foothills of Lohagad, close to the Navgraha temple area.Police had initially examined whether she had fallen from the fort or died due to another cause. Later reports attributed her death to suicide, allegedly linked to distress over health problems and her inability to appear for her LLB third-year examination.Facebook post allegedly led Goyal to LohagadThe chargesheet focuses on how information about Govindpurkar's death allegedly reached the accused.According to the prosecution, Goyal came across information about Govindpurkar's death on Facebook and later discussed the Lohagad location with Chaudhary.The two allegedly decided that Agarwal could be pushed from the fort, making his death appear to be an accidental fall. Police said the information about the location was also shared with Hange.Police allege that the accused then carried out further searches relating to Lohagad, trekking incidents and deaths involving falls in the Lonavala region.Investigators have submitted the digital material recovered during the probe to the court as part of the chargesheet.Contract killer plan allegedly came firstThe chargesheet also says the accused had explored other ways of eliminating Agarwal before settling on the Lohagad plan.According to police, they had allegedly attempted to arrange a contract killer but eventually decided to carry out the murder themselves.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: A Sydney shopper bought a carved cup for A$4 at a thrift shop; experts identified it as a centuries-old Chinese rhinoceros-horn cup, and was auctioned for A$75,640 in 2013
articles.summary: They say one man’s trash can be another man’s treasure. And that’s exactly what happened at a thrift shop in Sydney, Australia.
articles.body: They say one man’s trash can be another man’s treasure. And that’s exactly what happened at a thrift shop in Sydney, Australia.A regular shopper at the store saw a cup. It had a large chip in it.Not a hairline flaw you'd need to squint to see. A proper chip, the sort that should have been enough to send a shopper on to the next shelf in a Sydney op shop. The cup was priced at A$4. The shopper bought it anyway.The specialist who later valued it explained that pieces like this "don't look immediately attractive to the untrained eye". But something about the cup caught the buyer’s attention.The rare cup was eventually auctioned for A$75,640.An ordinary op-shop circuit, an extraordinary findThe buyer, who chose to stay anonymous, used to do the rounds of local op shops, which means he had seen plenty of shelves. But this one made him stop. He thought the cup looked a little special. He bought it. After the purchase, the man sent photographs to Ann Roberts, a Sotheby's consultant and specialist in Asian art, The Age reported.Roberts knew the cup was rare and valuable. The buyer had a one-of-a-kind cup. It was a Chinese libation cup carved from rhinoceros horn, catalogued as a ‘Magnolia and Prunus’ piece from the 17th or 18th century. Despite the large chip, she set a pre-sale estimate of A$20,000 to A$30,000. Finding such a rare piece in an op shop, according to the expert, is not something anyone should expect.And just like that, a A$4 cup fetched the buyer a five-figure sum!The rare cup was auctioned for A$75,640In 2013, the auction for the rare rhino cup started. The hammer fell at A$62,000 at the Sotheby's Australia auction in Melbourne. Along with the buyer’s premium, the final price came to A$75,640. The final price was more than twice Sotheby’s top estimate and 15,500 times the A$4 the shopper had paid.Roberts phoned the vendor to tell him the results, and he was thrilled. "He was very pleased,” she told the outlet. "It was a rare find. They don't look immediately attractive to the untrained eye."Sotheby's, however, didn’t identify the buyer of the rhino-horn cup. Such rare pieces are especially prized among Asian collectors. Though prized, items made from materials such as ivory and rhinoceros horn, even if more than 300 years old, require CITES licences to be sent overseas. But for the shopper who spotted the chipped cup on a thrift-store shelf, that A$4 find turned into a small fortune. Thrifters occasionally stumble upon treasures hiding in plain sight, but recognising their value is another matter. In this case, one shopper’s decision to take a second look turned an overlooked cup into a A$75,640 auction sale.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘Time for trial and error is over’: OpenAI safety employee David Robinson quits over AI risks
articles.summary: A former OpenAI safety employee has resigned from the company, warning that its rapid development of increasingly capable AI systems could raise the risk
articles.body: A former OpenAI safety employee has resigned from the company, warning that its rapid development of increasingly capable AI systems could raise the risk of serious failures. David Robinson said the “time for trial and error is over” and argued that AI companies need to put far greater emphasis on safety before developing more powerful systems.Robinson made the comments in an article titled "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken", published by The Atlantic on Saturday.Robinson said AI companies, including OpenAI, were not being "nearly careful enough" and argued that safety research and expertise should play a much bigger role before more powerful AI systems are developed.Robinson spent 3-1/2 years at OpenAI, where he helped draft the company's preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches. He said the company's focus on moving quickly from one AI model launch to another was making it difficult to maintain the level of caution he believed was necessary."As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed."He argued that the development of advanced AI should no longer rely on a process of repeatedly releasing systems, finding problems and fixing them afterwards.OpenAI refers to this approach as "iterative deployment", under which systems are released and their safeguards are strengthened as new problems are identified.Robinson argued that this approach is no longer sufficient as AI systems become more powerful."The time for trial and error is over," he wrote, saying advanced AI systems should have safeguards comparable to those used in high-risk fields such as nuclear power and aviation.His criticism comes amid a wider debate in the AI industry over whether companies are developing increasingly powerful systems faster than their ability to understand and control them. OpenAI and rival Anthropic have both faced scrutiny following incidents involving failed safety controls or unexpected behaviour from experimental AI systems.Robinson also warned that AI capabilities are advancing faster than researchers' understanding of alignment. AI alignment refers to efforts to ensure that AI systems behave in ways that are consistent with human goals and values.OpenAI defended its approach, saying it continues to put safety measures in place and can slow development when necessary."We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement.You use AI every day. articles.body: More than one civilian was killed or injured every 23 minutes on average in Ukraine during the first eight months of 2026.According to the Kyiv Independent, citing the UN Human Rights Office, civilian casualties during the period were 55 percent higher than in the same period last year. The figures include both people killed and injured in attacks across Ukraine.The rise comes as Russia has intensified its use of missiles, drones and aerial glide bombs, with attacks increasingly striking populated areas and critical infrastructure. Residential buildings, schools, medical facilities, railway infrastructure, shops and other civilian sites have been damaged or destroyed, putting people in densely populated areas at risk.Russia's expanding attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure have added another layer to the crisis. articles.summary: Hamam al-Hammami, the flydubai co-pilot accused of trying to crash a passenger jet bound for Tel Aviv, told investigators after the plane landed in Saudi
articles.body: Hamam al-Hammami, the flydubai co-pilot accused of trying to crash a passenger jet bound for Tel Aviv, told investigators after the plane landed in Saudi Arabia that he wanted to deliberately bring it down and was 'not afraid of death', according to a Wall Street Journal report.The 29-year-old Omani national is now under investigation as to how he became radicalised, and how someone whose extremist interests had already drawn the attention of authorities was later allowed back into the cockpit.From a love of flying to radicalisationAccording to the Wall Street Journal, Hammami's first aviation employer, state-owned Oman Air, banned him from flying after authorities discovered that he was visiting extremist websites.People briefed on his background told the newspaper that he was subsequently put through a deradicalisation programme and reassigned to a desk job.After leaving Oman Air, Hammami eventually found work in the UAE, and Flydubai hired him in February 2026. It remains unclear what information about his earlier history was available to the airline or whether Oman was ever asked to provide it. The WSJ reported that Oman received no requests from other countries for information to vet him for employment.Investigators are also looking at Hammami's time in Syria.Born to an Omani father and Syrian mother, Hammami spent part of his youth in Syria during the country's civil war. According to people familiar with the investigation cited by the WSJ, authorities are examining whether he began to radicalise while there, when Islamist rebels were fighting Bashar al-Assad's government.Hammami’s social media also provides a substantial online record that predates the flydubai attack.More than 3,000 screenshots from Hammami's deleted X account remain available through the Internet Archive.The posts include deeply conservative and misogynistic views, including statements opposing women working and expressing a preference for religious women who wear the veil.One post described Hammami creating a fake account to contact Saudi women. In another, he wrote that his wife should not work.The material does not by itself establish when he became violent or whether his views directly caused the flydubai attack. But investigators are examining the posts alongside his earlier extremist-web activity and his time in Syria to establish whether they form part of a broader process of radicalisation.The flydubai attackOn September 30, Hammami attacked Captain Smit Machchhar aboard flydubai Flight 1073, using a cockpit crash axe before trying to take control of the aircraft.The plane plunged more than 16,000 feet in roughly 30 seconds before the badly injured captain managed to open the cockpit door. Passengers and crew then overpowered Hammami, while two off-duty pilots on board helped stabilise and land the aircraft in Saudi Arabia.After the emergency landing, a Saudi official briefed on his interrogation told the WSJ that Hammami acknowledged that he wanted to deliberately crash the aircraft and was not afraid of death.The UAE, Saudi Arabia and Israel are investigating whether he acted alone or had links to outside groups, especially Iran.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Kalani DNA of crime’ vs ‘Manchekar gang member’: BJP-Sena war gets personal in Ulhasnagar
articles.summary: ULHASNAGAR: The BJP-Sena feud in Ulhasnagar has taken a sharp and personal turn, with the BJP alleging that the entry of people associated with the Kalani
articles.body: ULHASNAGAR: The BJP-Sena feud in Ulhasnagar has taken a sharp and personal turn, with the BJP alleging that the entry of people associated with the Kalani group — whom it described as having a “criminal DNA” — into the Shiv Sena was deliberately damaging the BJP-Sena alliance.All BJP's 37 corporators also unanimously declared that they will not work for Shiv Sena MP Dr Shrikant Shinde, son of Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde, from Kalyan Loksabha.In a counterattack, Shiv Sena leader and husband of Ulhasnagar mayor Ashwini Nikam, Kamlesh Nikam, directly targeted Maharashtra BJP president Ravindra Chavan, alleging that several criminal cases were registered against him and going a step further to describe him as a “member of the Manchekar gang”.The war of words follows the bitter dispute over the appointment of seven nominated corporators in the Ulhasnagar Municipal Corporation (UMC), with the local BJP leadership now deciding to end its alliance with the Shiv Sena in the civic body.However, the BJP's local decision is not a final decision on the alliance at the higher political level. The Ulhasnagar BJP unit has conveyed to its senior leadership that it does not want to continue the alliance with the Shiv Sena in the civic body.The final decision on whether the BJP will formally remain in an alliance with the Shiv Sena in the UMC will be taken by the party's top leadership.The local BJP leadership has decided to sit in the opposition in the civic body instead of continuing to work with the Sena. The decision was conveyed by BJP district president Rajesh Vadhrya, MLA Kumar Ailani and other local leaders following the nominated-corporator controversy.The BJP has also announced that its local unit will not cooperate with Kalyan Lok Sabha MP Dr Shrikant Shinde in future election-related work, further escalating tensions between the two Mahayuti partners.BJP leaders claimed that their differences were not with traditional Shiv Sena workers and that several old Shiv Sainiks continued to maintain good relations with the BJP. However, the BJP alleged that the entry of people associated with the Pappu Kalani group into the Shiv Sena had changed the political equation in Ulhasnagar.BJP leaders alleged that after people associated with the Kalani group entered the Sena and Ashwini Nikam became mayor, decisions in the civic body were being taken in a manner detrimental to the BJP.The BJP specifically targeted the nominated-corporator appointment process, alleging that despite having 37 corporators, it was given only two of the seven nominated posts, while the Sena and its supporters secured five. The BJP has said it will challenge the mayor's decision in court.The Shiv Sena has rejected the BJP's allegations and launched a counterattack. Arun Ashan, group leader of Shiv Sena in UMC said the BJP claiming that it would not work for Shrikant Shinde, but alleged that BJP leaders had not extended full support to Shinde even during the previous election.Ashan claimed that the Shiv Sena had supported BJP MLA candidates including Sulabha Gaikwad, Ravindra Chavan and Kumar Ailani during their respective elections. He warned that if the BJP-Sena confrontation continued, the Shiv Sena would work against the BJP's three MLAs in the next election.Meanwhile Nikam directly targeted state BJP president Ravindra Chavan. He alleged that while the BJP was accusing people associated with the Kalani group of having criminal backgrounds, Chavan himself was linked to the “Manchekar gang” and described him as a “member” of the group.Nikam demanded that Chavan be removed as state BJP president, claiming that his continuation in the post would further widen the differences between the two alliance partners. The allegations against Chavan were made by Nikam and have not been independently established.After Shiv Sena's press conference, BJP Ulhasnagar district president Rajesh Vadhrya again hold press conference and hit back at Nikam, saying the Kamlesh Nikam had no standing to make allegations against the state BJP president. Vadhrya said the BJP would demonstrate its position through action rather than statements.Vadhrya also levelled allegations against former Ulhasnagar MLA Pappu Kalani, claiming that Kalani was sentenced life imprisonment till death but had secured release from prison after submitting a false health report. Vadhrya further alleged that cases had been registered against Omie Kalani, Kamlesh Nikam and Manoj Lassi.The latest confrontation began with the appointment of seven nominated corporators in the UMC. The BJP had argued that its numerical strength entitled it to four of the seven positions, while the Shiv Sena should have received three. However, two BJP nominees and five Sena nominees were ultimately declared by Mayor.The BJP has challenged the process and alleged that the mayor's decision was contrary to the numerical strength of the parties. The Sena's position is that of the four candidates proposed by the BJP, only two were valid, while the remaining positions were filled through the prescribed process.The dispute escalated further on Saturday night when BJP office-bearers, angered by Kamlesh Nikam’s personal remarks against the state BJP president threatened Nikam to teach lessons reach near his residence.Police reached the spot soon after. A short while later, Shiv Sena workers also assembled outside the residence in support of Nikam, leading to a tense atmosphere for some time. The police subsequently increased security in the area, after which members of both groups left the spot.With the local BJP unit deciding to withdraw from the civic alliance and sit in opposition, the dispute has now moved beyond the nominated-corporator issue.For now, the local BJP leadership has conveyed its decision to end the civic-level alliance to the party's senior leadership. Whether the BJP formally ends its alliance with the Shiv Sena in the UMC will depend on the decision of the party's top leadership.The episode has also opened a new front between the two Mahayuti partners, with BJP leaders targeting the Kalani group and Sena leaders directly attacking the state BJP leadership.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: ‘I came for a degree, ended up wanting to stay’: Zimbabwean student’s adorable love letter to India wins hearts
articles.summary: What if moving to another country for a degree leaves you wanting to stay forever?
articles.body: What if moving to another country for a degree leaves you wanting to stay forever?That seems to be what happened with Zimbabwean student Kalumba Mwale, whose post about his time in India has caught attention online. He described coming to India to study as a “mistake”, but anyone reading the rest of his post quickly realises that he wasn't complaining.Quite the opposite.For Mwale, what started as a decision to pursue an education turned into three years of food, travel, friendships and experiences that changed the way he looked at India.So, why did he call it a ‘mistake’?Mwale shared his experience on Instagram, explaining that India became much more than the place where he happened to study.“I came here for a degree… and ended up wanting to stay. India became much more than just the country where I studied,” he wrote.And then came his list of reasons.One of the first things he mentioned was food.Mwale said he had got used to how affordable eating out can be in India, to the point that he now looks at food prices back home differently.He also singled out UPI as something he didn't realise he'd miss so much.“UPI completely spoiled me. I can pay for chai, food, transport and almost anything with my phone,” he wrote.For someone used to paying for everyday things this way, going back to a different payment system can apparently feel like a step backwards.Biryani, butter chicken, dosa and momosThen there was the food.Mwale said he had become “addicted” to Indian food, naming biryani, butter chicken, dosa and momos among his favourites.And it wasn't just about eating.Travelling around India became another big part of his experience. Despite spending three years in the country, Mwale said he felt he had barely seen enough of it.“Even after three years, I feel like I’ve barely scratched the surface of India,” he wrote.From one region to another, he found himself experiencing different food, languages, traditions and ways of life.India became more than a study destinationPerhaps the biggest change, however, came from the people he met.Mwale said studying in India introduced him to people from different parts of the country as well as students from countries he never expected to meet.“Studying in India exposed me to different Indian cultures, languages and people from countries I never expected to meet,” he wrote.That experience appears to have changed his idea of what home means too.“I came here as a Zimbabwean student. Somewhere along the way, India became a place I genuinely feel connected to,” Mwale said.So the “mistake” wasn't really a mistake.He later clarified that he was being sarcastic. In fact, he described these experiences as some of the best things that happened because he chose to study in India.He came for a degree.But according to him, he ended up with much more: friendships, memories, travel experiences and a connection to a country he hadn't expected to call home.‘India is like a second home’The post drew plenty of warm reactions online, with Indian users welcoming Mwale and relating to his experience.“It’s always heartwarming to hear someone born abroad say they love the country I was born in,” one person commented.Another told him, “I think India is like a second home for you now!” and even suggested that he learn to cook Indian food or make reels around it.“Whoever comes to India once becomes a part of India forever,” another comment read.A user added, “Welcome, brother. If you welcome the change, you can treat India like a second home.”For Mwale, perhaps that's the real story behind the word “mistake”. He arrived in India expecting an education. Three years later, he found himself wondering if he wanted to leave at all.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: How two brothers put the humble handpan on Bengluru’s musical map
articles.summary: Twenty-six handpans turned a Bengaluru festival stage into a sea of metallic sound.
articles.body: Twenty-six handpans turned a Bengaluru festival stage into a sea of metallic sound. At the centre of the 24-member ensemble were brothers, Ranganathan S, 15, and Sriniketan S, 11. They had spent months rehearsing, travelling across the city several times a week and helping coordinate compositions for the ensemble.At its debut public performance at Bengaluru's Ganesha Utsava, the ensemble played five songs with 26 handpans alongside mridangam, ghatam, drums, guitar, synth and djembe. Their repertoire included Carnatic compositions along with 'Varaha Roopam' from the film 'Kantara.'Led by the Nadamaya Brothers, who were playing two handpans each, the performance offered the city's growing handpan community an opportunity to demonstrate that an instrument still on the fringes of mainstream music can function as a lead instrument. Their journey began during the pandemic.Ranganathan, who was nine then, had already been experimenting with the keyboard when a neighbour invited him to see an unusual percussion instrument he had begun crafting.His first impression remains vivid. "It looked like a spaceship," he recalls. Intrigued by its shape and sound, he quickly picked up the basics. Within a few hours, he was exploring melodies on an instrument he had never encountered before. Soon, his younger brother followed.Sriniketan says he was initially drawn to the instrument because his elder brother was playing it. "I was inspired by watching my brother play the handpan. I have been learning to play the handpan for the past three years now. What I love most is that it combines percussion and melody, so you can play both at once without needing two separate instruments," he says.Today, both brothers practise for at least two hours every day, often spending considerably longer when preparing for a public performance. Ranganathan, having completed his Class 10 examinations ahead of schedule, has taken a gap year to focus entirely on music, combining handpan practice with Carnatic vocal training and Vedic studies.Age, however, is not the only reason why the brothers have attracted attention within the handpan community. Fellow performers describe them as among the country's most accomplished young handpan players. While other ensemble members handle rhythmic and harmonic layers, the brothers perform the lead melodies, navigating complex arrangements and Carnatic-inspired compositions on chromatic handpans carrying more than 40 notes.Their rise mirrors the growth of Bengaluru's handpan community itself.At the centre of this growth is Chirag Vaitheeswaran, founder of Chirp Handpans, regarded by the handpan community as one of India's pioneering indigenous handpan makers. His fascination with the instrument began in 2013, when he encountered one on a beach in Gokarna. At the time, handpans were difficult to obtain, with long international waiting lists and high import costs.He embarked on a painstaking quest to build one himself while working at Microsoft. For nearly two years, he estimates that he produced nearly 200 failed shells before crafting a successful instrument. His Bengaluru workshop now employs 14 artisans and has delivered more than 1,300 instruments crafted entirely from Indian-sourced materials.Making the instrument accessible contributed to the growth of Bengaluru's handpan community through workshops and impromptu jam sessions. Players began looking beyond the instrument's familiar association with meditation, yoga retreats, and ambient soundscapes."I truly believe this instrument has the power to touch people across age groups and backgrounds, and I'm excited to be part of a community that's helping introduce it to more people," says ensemble member, Shruthi Shetty.The ensemble itself is designed to highlight the melodic and rhythmic capabilities of the handpan, with different performers assigned roles like those in an orchestra. The arrangement, inspired partly by steel-pan ensembles in Trinidad and Tobago, seeks to demonstrate that the instrument can support complex musical performances rather than simply create atmosphere. That vision resonates strongly with Ranganathan.His ambition is to take Indian handpan music to international audiences and expand its repertoire through Carnatic music, film songs and original compositions. He believes familiarity is key: audiences first recognise a song and then begin paying attention to the instrument producing it. "If it stays in the background, it won't become famous," says the teenager. "I want it to become like the flute or the mandolin."What is a handpan?The handpan is still an unfamiliar instrument for many people. Resembling a metallic flying saucer, it is played entirely with the hands and produces deep, resonant tones that blend melody and rhythm. The handpan is tuned to a specific scale, allowing even first-time players to create harmonious sounds, making it accessible.Origin: Inspired by the steelpan from Trinidad and Tobago, as well as traditional instruments like the Indian ghatam and Indonesian gamelan, people across the world started refining and creating their own versions of handpans. The creators combined elements of the Caribbean steelpan (steel drum) with the Indian ghatam (a clay pot percussion instrument, mostly used in Carnatic music).Meaning of its name: "Hang" means "hand" in the Bernese German dialect, describing how the instrument is played.Material: It is built from two glued-together steel shells made of a treated metal, called nitrided steel.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Bengaluru woman's 17-breakdown traffic tale: 19-km journey takes 3 hours as she races to catch train
articles.summary: BENGALURU: A woman's frantic three-hour journey to cover just 19km through peak-hour Bengaluru traffic has drawn attention online after she shared a video
articles.body: BENGALURU: A woman's frantic three-hour journey to cover just 19km through peak-hour Bengaluru traffic has drawn attention online after she shared a video recounting how she raced against time to catch a train to Kerala.The woman said she started from Electronic City around 5pm to catch a 7pm train from Krishnarajapuram station, despite knowing that the train was already running two hours late.Heavy rain in Bengaluru further worsened the traffic, stretching what should have been a short journey into a three-hour ordeal.She said the 19km journey took more than three hours, leaving her and her fellow travellers convinced midway that they would miss the train.Bengaluru traffic puts train journey at riskAccording to her account, the worsening traffic led them to consider turning back. However, they noticed that the train was being held up at some stations, giving them a chance to still make it."We were like head on head with the train kind of," she said, recalling how their journey and the train's progress seemed to be racing against each other.By the time they reached the station, the train was being announced for platform number two. She said they rushed out of the cab with their suitcases and ran up and down the stairs to reach the train. ‘Running as if we were running for our life’The woman said the journey was particularly important as the upcoming long weekend meant getting another ticket to Kerala in the next three days would have been difficult."We had to travel and that's why we were running as if we were running for our life," she said.She said it was only after they boarded the train that they were able to relax.Woman’s 17-breakdown traffic taleIn the caption accompanying the video, she summed up the experience with humour: "19 km. 3 hours. One train to catch. And approximately 17 emotional breakdowns in between.""At one point I had already accepted that the train was gone and Bangalore had won. But somehow… SOMEHOW… I made it. " she wrote.She added: "Peak Bangalore traffic really said, ‘You wanted a peaceful journey? Not today.’" ‘Huge respect’ for Bengaluru commutersThe experience also left her expressing admiration for people who make long daily commutes through Bengaluru's traffic.She said she was not someone who could handle such a journey every day and had, over the last 10 years, tried to live within five kilometres of her workplace."Hopefully I can do it," she said, referring to continuing to stay close to work.She also hoped for better transport and road infrastructure in Bengaluru, while ending on a softer note about the city."whatever I complain about Bangalore I still love you Bangalore," she said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news.
